thread:
jess: Noticed a pretty bad drop in prefix cache hit-rate on Private deployments after last week's runtime push.

jess: From our dashboards: private clusters in eu-west showing prefix_cache_hit_rate falling ~82% -> ~50% after 2026-03-09 roll.

jess: Quick 5m rollup snapshot: 
```
prefix_cache_lookups=1,150,000
prefix_cache_hits=575,000
prefix_cache_hit_rate=0.5
avg_kv_fetch_ms_private=31.2
avg_kv_fetch_ms_dedicated=4.1
kv_io_errors_inc=0.8%
```

carlos: Yikes. Any differences in cache client/storage between hosted/dedicated/private? Could be config drift or backend mismatch.

jess: Yes: hosted -> in-process LRU. dedicated -> local RocksDB (NVMe) behind kv-proxy. private -> NFS-mounted store in customer VPCs, some via S3-gateway adapters. We're seeing higher fetch latencies and occasional transient resets hitting the NFS layer.

anya: Two suspects: 1) key cardinality increased (so fewer reuses), 2) backend latency causes eviction before reuse. What are keys currently including? session, tenant, model?

marcus: We shipped a change in v0.23.1 where cache_key template added ${session_id} to isolate sessions. It shipped to Private first. That massively increases cardinality.

li: Combine that with NFS fetch ms ~30+ and you'll never reuse an entry. Suggest revert to less granular keying (model+prefix hash) + use namespace per tenant.

jess: Current runtime config snippet: 
```
cache_key: "redwood:kv:${model}:${session_id}:${sha256(prefix)}"
cache_ttl_seconds: 3600
eviction_policy: lru
```

jess: Proposed temp change for Private: 
```
cache_key: "redwood:kv:${model}:${sha256(prefix)}"
cache_namespace: "tenant:${tenant_id}"
cache_ttl_seconds: 7200
```

carlos: Also discovered client gRPC keepalive changes in the same release: aggressive keepalives + short timeouts. For Private VPCs behind strict NAT/GW that can cause reconnect storms and higher kv fetch latency.

anya: Can we quickly repro fetch latency from an affected private node? Simple loop hitting local runtime/kv fetch will show p50/p99.

marcus: I ran a smoke: median ~28ms, p99 ~130ms on private. Dedicated medians are <5ms. So network/storage is the main axis, but keying change amplifies the problem.

ops-bot: Incident automation: created ticket INF-2026-37. Alert rule configured to page if prefix_cache_hit_rate < 60% for >10m.

li: Immediate mitigations (short term):
- revert inclusion of session_id in cache_key for Private
- increase cache_ttl and add sharded LRU to reduce eviction churn
- relax gRPC keepalive frequency and enable connection pooling

jess: Medium-term ideas:
- node startup pre-warm: fetch top-k prefixes per model into node-local memory (avoid writing warmup payloads to NFS)
- off-peak synthetic warmup job that replays high-frequency prefixes into Private clusters
- add metrics: cache_warmup_latency, prefix_miss_ratio_by_storage

carlos: Warmup should be read-only: populate node-local in-memory cache or local SSD fallback, not hammer the backend with writes. Also consider a tiny local SSD cache for Private nodes as fallback when NFS is slow.

anya: Related batching point: larger batching mixes prefixes and reduces per-prefix reuse. We might route latency-sensitive, single-prefix traffic to warmed nodes and batch other traffic separately.

marcus: Also correlate with kernel selection changes in v0.23.1: we enabled an experimental attention kernel that slightly increased per-token compute for short sequences. Cache misses + slower kernel -> worse tail latency. Need to tag traces for kernel variant and cache-miss events.

jess: Action items (owner -> ETA):
- revert session_id key change for Private (marcus) -> ASAP
- patch gRPC keepalive + pooling defaults (carlos) -> EOD
- add warmup job + telemetry: cache_warmup_latency, prefix_miss_ratio (anya) -> PR by Thu
- run SSD-fallback A/B on Private vs Dedicated (li + infra) -> next week

li: I'll also add a small dashboard breakdown: inproc / nvme / nfs / s3-gateway so we can track regressions per storage type.

marcus: Pausing private channel in the release and opening rollback PR now.

jess: Thanks all. For repro folks, quick warmup generator we used: 
```
python tools/top_prefixes.py --logs logs/requests.log --top 1000 --out prefixes.json
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/_internal/warmup -d @prefixes.json
```

ops-bot: Noted. Updating incident INF-2026-37 with links to perf traces: https://perf.internal/redwood/traces/tx/1745154321

carlos: Will follow up after keepalive patch and rollback.

jess: I'll post results in this thread after revert/telemetry. Thanks :heart:
